hubMainHtml:
Investment and Financial Literacy

Start with the two concepts that drive most long-term financial outcomes: compounding and inflation.

This is a collection of beginner-friendly articles that make finance and investing understandable with plain language and explicit assumptions.

Featured Concepts

Compound Interest: The Ultimate Wealth Builder

Why compounding is the single most powerful force in long-term investing.

Inflation: The Math That Makes Future Money Smaller

Why purchasing power declines over time and why returns must be inflation-adjusted.

Core Concepts

Start here for the basic ideas behind investing and markets.

  • What Is Investing?

    A simple definition for beginners and new investors. What investing is, why people invest, and how time can work in your favor.

  • Investing vs Trading: Key Differences Explained

    Investing and trading are fundamentally different activities. Learn how they differ in time horizon, taxes, costs, skill set, and long-term arithmetic.

  • Investing with Leverage: When Borrowed Money Works For You — and When It Doesn't

    Mortgages, margin, leveraged ETFs, and the Smith Manoeuvre: how borrowed money amplifies gains and losses, and when the bad scenario breaks the strategy.

  • How Does a Mortgage Work in Canada?

    Principal vs interest, term vs amortization, fixed vs variable, down payments, stress tests, renewal risk — and why total cost matters more than the monthly payment.

  • Pay Off Your Mortgage Faster or Invest?

    Compare accelerated mortgage paydown versus investing the same extra cash using break-even returns, time horizon, fees, and registered accounts.

  • What Is a Stock? (In Simple Terms)

    What a share represents, how stocks make money, and why stock prices move — explained with simple arithmetic.

  • What Is the Stock Market?

    What the stock market is, how it works, and why it can grow over time.

  • Asset Classes for Investing

    The major asset classes — stocks, bonds, cash, and real assets — and why asset allocation matters.

  • Dollar Cost Averaging: What It Is, How It Works, and When It Makes Sense

    What DCA is, how it works, lump sum vs. DCA, the behavioural case for automatic investing, and common misunderstandings.

  • What "XEQT and Chill" Really Means — The Arithmetic Behind Low-Cost ETF Investing

    What the phrase means, how fee arithmetic drives the approach, and when it does not fit.

Time and Compounding

How time and compounding interact with fees, costs, and long horizons.

  • The True Cost of Financial Advisor Fees

    How advisory fees, fund costs, and lost compounding interact over decades.

Accounts and Rules (Canada)

How Canadian registered accounts and withdrawal rules change the arithmetic.

  • What Is a TFSA? Tax-Free Savings Account Explained (Canada)

    Contribution room, the January 1 withdrawal rule, what you can hold inside, and why tax-free growth matters.

  • What Is an RRSP? Registered Retirement Savings Plan Explained (Canada)

    How the tax deduction works, why tax-sheltered growth matters, and how to think about RRSP vs TFSA using the math.

  • RRSP vs TFSA vs FHSA in Canada: Which Account Is Best?

    Compare tax math, contribution limits, and worked examples across RRSP, TFSA, and FHSA.

  • What Is an FHSA? First Home Savings Account Explained (Canada)

    How the FHSA works, its tax treatment, limits, and interaction with other accounts.

  • What Is a Non-Registered Account? Taxable Investing in Canada, Explained

    How interest, dividends, and capital gains are taxed outside registered accounts, tax drag, asset location, and what usually belongs in a taxable account.

  • TFSA Withdrawal Rules: The January 1 Rule and Over-Contribution Penalties

    Why withdrawn TFSA room returns on January 1, how over-contributions happen, and how penalties are calculated.

  • Norbert's Gambit: How Canadian Investors Convert CAD to USD Without Paying Hidden Currency Fees (2026 Guide)

    How to convert CAD to USD (and back) at the real market exchange rate, avoid hidden brokerage FX spreads, and when the strategy is worth using.
